extracted.intended_audience: public information professionals / PIOs with at least 2 years of public information experience; emergency management personnel seeking advanced PIO training
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines and requirements for applying to, attending, and completing the NDEMU E0388 Advanced Public Information Officer (Advanced PIO) 5-day classroom course, including prerequisites, delivery types, and administrative/registration rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Target audience / eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: The 0388 Advanced Public Information Officer course is open to participants who have a minimum of 2 years of public information experience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Designed for public information professionals with at least 2 years of experience and who have completed the listed prerequisites.

rubrics_metrics.name: Course length and mandatory attendance
rubrics_metrics.description: Course Length: 5 days (40 hours). Attendance during each day of the course is mandatory.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Advanced PIO program consists solely of the 0388 classroom course comprising 5 days (40 hours) of collaborative learning; participants must attend every day.

rubrics_metrics.name: Course objectives / learning outcomes
rubrics_metrics.description: Participants will gain the knowledge and skills to establish, manage and operate within a Joint Information Center (JIC), including strategic communications and incident action planning as it relates to JIC operations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The advanced level course teaches additional skills for escalating incidents and includes a multi-day functional exercise (FE) to apply advanced public information skills and to assess participants' abilities to analyze, coordinate, process and create information in a fast-paced, realistic environment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Classroom course delivery types
rubrics_metrics.description: E0388: Classroom Delivery — Resident (E), Local (L), Virtual (K).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each delivery type may have unique registration requirements depending on the host. Field (L) deliveries often require registration through the state's training system and separate online application with NDEMU to receive credit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required prerequisites (must be completed prior to application)
rubrics_metrics.description: The following 8 independent study courses, plus 1 classroom course (E/L/K 0105), must be completed in their entirety prior to submitting an application to 0388: IS29, E/L/K 0105, IS42, IS100, IS200, IS247 or IS251, IS700, IS800 and IS2900.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These prerequisites include the Basic & Awareness Level PIO courses. The page states: 'There are 9 required prerequisites listed below which satisfy the requirements to apply for the 0388 course.' Many prerequisite courses accept 'any version'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recommended prerequisites
rubrics_metrics.description: Seven highly recommended prerequisites that will greatly benefit participants: E0300 (ICS 300), IS-120, IS-201 (forms used for IAP; waived if ICS300 completed), IS-242, IS-650, IS-660, and IS-909.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are recommended (not required) but noted as greatly beneficial to participants; some courses have substitutions or waivers (e.g., IS-201 waived if ICS300 completed).

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-course work requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Some pre-course work is required prior to the training course.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Participants should complete assigned pre-course work before the start of the classroom course (specific pre-course work details not listed on this page).

rubrics_metrics.name: Device requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Participants must bring a laptop with internet capabilities for daily course activities (tablets or cell phones can be used as a secondary device not a primary device).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A laptop is required as the primary device for course activities each day.

rubrics_metrics.name: Withdrawal / last-minute cancellation policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Withdrawals or last-minute cancellations within 15 days of course start date will incur a one-year probation period for future APIO applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should avoid last-minute cancellations to prevent being placed on a one-year probation for future Advanced PIO applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application and approval process
rubrics_metrics.description: All NDEMU applications require an electronic approval from the head of your sponsoring organization. You will need the name, title, and email address of this person to submit the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants are instructed: 'Please use the email of your Supervisor as the Head of Organization for approval on the Online Application.' Application status notifications will be sent to the email address provided during application. Apply online at NETC Online Admissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Registration path differences for field deliveries
rubrics_metrics.description: Field deliveries (L0388) require registration through the host state's training system; after registering with the State, applicants should apply online with NDEMU to receive credit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For field deliveries use the contact info listed for that delivery as the Head of Organization approval on the Online Application. Each field delivery lists local contact info and state registration links.

rubrics_metrics.name: Course codes and location/contact instructions
rubrics_metrics.description: Each offering has a code (e.g., E0388 for Resident, L0388 for Field) and specific location/contact information listed for each scheduled delivery.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the listed contact (program manager or state training officer) for questions and follow the registration instructions provided for the specific delivery; the page lists multiple scheduled dates, locations, and local contacts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acceptable versions for prerequisite courses
rubrics_metrics.description: Many prerequisite independent study courses are acceptable in 'Any version' (e.g., IS-42, IS-100, IS-200, IS-247/IS-251, IS-700, IS-800, IS-2900).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page explicitly notes 'Any version' for many of the listed prerequisite courses; check course details if version matters for your credentialing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Functional exercise participation requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Participants will have the opportunity to apply advanced public information skills during a multi-day functional exercise designed to assess and challenge abilities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The FE is integrated into the 5-day course to test skills to analyze, coordinate, process, and create information in a fast-paced, realistic environment; active participation is implied as part of course completion.
